analysis.title: GS Sharkey - US Equities Mid Day Color 7 Oct 2026
key_insights: Index-level session was muted (SPX intraday band 43bps) but the rotation underneath was sharp. Russell underperformed NDX for the 4th straight day and 17 of the last 20 sessions, as small caps bear the brunt of higher rates.

Sector moves point to defensive positioning: Healthcare, Staples and Utilities outperformed. Hedge funds were still adding to risk, with the GS Most Short basket down -130bps, and ETF volumes were light.
Fed minutes this afternoon are the next catalyst. A hawkish tone could extend the bond selloff and add pressure to equities ahead of bank earnings next week.

High beta proxies reversed after yesterday's leadership: Rare Earths (GSXURARE) -5.5%, Robotics (GSXUROBO) -3%, Uranium (GSXURANI) -3.5%. The PowerUp America basket (GSENEPOW) gave back -2% after its 3rd best day in the last 5 years.
Financials earnings start next Tuesday, with JPM, C and WFC reporting in the morning. The desk published a season preview covering focus areas, positioning, sentiment and performance.
Prime brokerage data from yesterday: US equities were net bought, with long buying and short covering in roughly equal amounts. Buying came from both Macro Products and Single Names.

GS franchise flow: activity was down -3% vs the trailing two weeks and market volumes were flat vs the 10-day moving average. The floor was -9% better for sale, driven by long-only clients, and the hedge fund short ratio was at a 2-week high.

Long-only clients were -25% better for sale, with large sell skews in Macro Products and Tech, and muted demand in Staples and Industrials. Hedge funds were -8% better for sale, with short supply most elevated in Utilities, Energy and Industrials.

Chart of the day: the GS Consumer Experiences Basket (GSXUCEXP) has underperformed SPXXAI even though spending growth on experiences rose from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026, vs 2% for broader services. GS sees it as well positioned if oil stays elevated or in a de-escalation scenario, and expects its correlation with AI to turn more positive.
